sources: Names, descriptions and grades: Exophase (Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophies). PSN progress targets: PSNProfiles (trophies 43531). Guides: written for this page from the official descriptions; where a place or step is not pinned down by a source, the guide says so.

phases.title: Story
phases.blurb: Chapters 1 to 4 and the finale. Story trophies unlock as the plot advances; save before the last mission.
phases.goal: Finish the story and unlock every chapter trophy; save before the finale.

phases.title: Stranger strands
phases.blurb: Leonida's strangers each have a chain of jobs to finish, ending in one last mission for each of them.
phases.goal: Meet all eight strangers and finish each one's chain.

phases.title: Activities
phases.blurb: Try everything once, then grind the counted ones: the range, drone races, fishing, bowling, meditation and the challenge list.
phases.goal: Try every activity, then master the counted ones.

phases.title: Collectibles and exploration
phases.blurb: All 52 areas of the map, the card sets, 100 WAiNK spots, 100 vehicles found and 10 registered.
phases.goal: See all 52 areas and pick up every card set.

phases.title: Crime and partner
phases.blurb: Robberies, escapes and partner work. The timing-sensitive trophies are here — save before every attempt.
phases.goal: Clear the robberies and partner jobs; save before the timed ones.

phases.title: Money and property
phases.blurb: Wash marked bills, spend $100,000 across the shops and buy all eight garages.
phases.goal: Wash the marked bills, spend across the shops and buy all eight garages.

phases.title: 100% cleanup and platinum
phases.blurb: Clear what the checklist still shows, hit 100% completion, and the platinum is yours.
phases.goal: Mop up the last counts, reach 100% and take the platinum.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.brief: The platinum: earn the other 54 and this unlocks on its own.
trophies.guide: There is nothing extra to do for the platinum itself — it pops the moment the 54th other trophy is earned. Treat it as the checklist's finish line, not a task. The real work is the two golds: the final mission and 100% completion. Clear the phases in order and this will be waiting at the end.
steps: Work the seven roadmap phases in order, ticking trophies off as they pop.
Save 100% completion for last — when it pops, the platinum pops with it.
trophies.tip: Sort the list by difficulty when only a few are left and clear the easy ones first for momentum.
trophies.prep: Nothing to prepare — this unlocks on its own at the end.
trophies.risk: Not missable. It unlocks on its own once the other 54 are earned, at any point in the game.
sources: Exophase: GTA VI PSN trophy list — names, descriptions, grades

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.brief: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the game's opening mission, so this is likely the first trophy you earn. It teaches movement, driving and the partner system as you play it — just follow the objectives to the results screen. Failing an attempt costs nothing; replay the mission and finish it.
steps: Start the story and follow the opening mission's objectives.
Reach the results screen; the trophy pops on completion.
trophies.tip: Play the opening as a tutorial — there is no reason to rush it.
trophies.prep: Nothing to prepare — the opening teaches as it goes.
trophies.risk: Safe if missions can be replayed. Replay has not been confirmed in the game yet, so finish it cleanly the first time.
sources: Exophase: GTA VI PSN trophy list — names, descriptions, grades

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.brief: Play through every mission in Chapter 1.
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes when its last mission ends, and the trophy lands with it. Stick to the story missions and leave the side content for later — the chapter only ends when its missions do. The official description does not name the closing mission, so check the in-game chapter screen to see what is left.
steps: Follow the story missions in the order the game offers them.
Finish the chapter's last mission; the trophy pops as the chapter ends.
trophies.tip: Check the chapter screen between missions so a side detour does not delay the ending.
trophies.prep: Nothing to prepare — just play the story missions.
trophies.risk: Nothing in the description makes this missable, as long as chapters can be replayed — replay is still unconfirmed in-game.

steps: Play Chapter 2's story missions in order.
Finish the chapter's closing mission to close the chapter.
trophies.tip: Stock up on supplies before the chapter's bigger jobs; the difficulty climbs from here.

Play the chapter through to its end; the trophy pops with the chapter close.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.brief: Reach 100% completion — the last big gold before the platinum.
trophies.guide: 100% completion is the long tail of the platinum: every story mission, every stranger strand, every activity count, every collectible and every counted thing on this checklist, finished. It is not a single task but the sum of the other 53 trophies plus whatever the in-game 100% counter asks for that no trophy names. Work the seven phases in order and let this counter climb on its own; only when it stalls should you chase what is left. What exactly counts toward 100% is not spelled out in the official trophy description, so this guide does not pretend to list it — the in-game stats screen is the authority.
steps: Clear the seven roadmap phases in order.
When the counter stalls, open the in-game stats screen and chase the categories still short.
Finish the last remaining item; the trophy pops with 100%.
trophies.tip: Do the counted grinds alongside other trophies — one drive can feed several counts at once.
trophies.prep: Nothing to prepare — it fills up as you clear the phases.
trophies.risk: Not missable. Completion is a counter, not a one-shot attempt; it only climbs.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.brief: Complete 250 stunts across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Stunts are the game's driving tricks — jumps, drifts, near-misses and the like — and the counter wants 250 of them. The official description does not define which moves count as a stunt, and the exact list is not confirmed in-game yet, so this guide does not invent one. In practice, treat every jump, drift and close call as progress, and watch the PSN counter climb. Ramps and long straight roads with traffic are the natural places to stack them.
steps: Drive aggressively: jumps, drifts and near-misses all feed the counter.
Use ramps and open roads to chain stunts; check the PSN counter as you go.
Keep going until the counter reads 250.
trophies.tip: A stunt that also feeds another trophy's count is worth twice as much — chase overlaps.
trophies.prep: Bring a fast car and find ramps and open roads.
trophies.risk: Not missable. Stunts can be done anywhere, any time, as many times as it takes.

trophies.brief: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Forty-two shooting challenges, and every one needs a gold medal — this is the hardest activity grind on the list. The range challenges test accuracy, speed and weapon handling, and the gold bar for each is set by the game. No challenge list is published in the official description, so none is given here; the in-game range shows which challenges are left and what gold requires. Work through them weapon by weapon, and replay any challenge as often as it takes — the range never closes.
steps: Visit the Shooting Range and open its challenge list.
Work the challenges weapon by weapon, replaying each until gold.
The trophy pops when the 42nd challenge turns gold.
trophies.tip: Learn one weapon's recoil at a time — gold is about consistency, not speed.
trophies.prep: Practise one weapon at a time before chasing gold.
trophies.risk: Not missable. Range challenges can be replayed without limit.
